Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 08/10/2024
1.

This is the first bail application filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail to the applicant, who has been arrested on 23.04.2024 in connection with Crime No. 124/2024 registered at Police Station- Bilaigarh, District- Sarangarh-Bilaigarh (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Section 363, 366(A), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 4 & 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The case of the prosecution, in brief, is that on 22.04.2024 victim's father lodged complaint before concerned police station alleging that on 06.04.2024, the applicant allured his minor daughter and took her to Digitally signed by ARUN Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh and made forceful physical relationship with ARUN KUMAR KUMAR DEWANGAN DEWANGAN
On 21.04.2024 at about 8.00 pm.
the applicant left her daughter on +0530 main road and ran away.

The statement of the victim was recorded before police and on the basis of her statement, the offence as aforestated Aryan Kumar Kurre vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140282149/
1 has been registered against the applicant.

sentences.text: 3. In pursuance of direction issued by this Court, the victim was present before this Court on 02.09.2024 along with her father through concerned DLSA and has raised objection in granting bail to the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He would further submit that the victim has not supported case of the prosecution and she was consenting party in commission of offence as such it cannot be termed as rape.

He would further submit that victim's mother examined before trial court, wherein she has stated that her marriage was solemnized when she was 18 years old and the victim took birth after one year of marriage and now victim's mother is 38 years old, therefore, it can be said that presently the victim is 18-19 years old.
He would further submit that there is nothing in the FSL report against the applicant.
He would further submit that the applicant is in jail since 23.04.2024 and the trial is likely to take some time for its final disposal.
Hence, it is prayed that this applicant may be enlarged on bail.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposing the bail application would submit that there is clear allegation against the applicant regarding commission of offence.
He would further submit that victim's father has stated that the applicant took his daughter for entertainment wherein he has made forcefully physical relationship with her.
The victim in her statement has narrated the incident and stated that the applicant took her and made forcefully physical relation with her and on 22.04.2024 left her on road.
Hence, the application for grant of bail may be rejected.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary with utmost satisfaction.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, material available against the applicant in the case diary, statement of the victim wherein she has supported case of the prosecution and also the material available in the medical report against the applicant, I am of the view that it is not a fit case, in which, the applicant should be enlarged on bail.
8. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. is rejected.
Certified copy, as per rules.
